summary: Open protocol that lets AI agents built on different frameworks discover each other and work together, with SDKs for Python, JS, Go, Java, .NET and Rust.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: A2A (Agent2Agent) is an open standard for communication between AI agents. Agents publish Agent Cards describing what they can do and how to connect, then exchange text, files and structured data over JSON-RPC 2.0 on HTTP(S), with request/response, streaming (SSE) and async push notifications. Agents can collaborate without revealing their internal memory, logic or tools.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agents built with different frameworks and vendors can't easily talk to each other. A2A gives them a shared protocol.
whoFor: Platform teams connecting agents across vendors
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for an open, community-driven standard with official SDKs in six languages and an enterprise focus on security, auth and observability.
requirements: One of the official SDKs for your language

overview: This repo holds the protocol specification. Start with the documentation site at a2a-protocol.org for an overview, the spec, tutorials and guides.
Official SDKs: Python (pip install a2a-sdk), Go, JavaScript (npm install @a2a-js/sdk), Java (Maven), .NET (NuGet) and Rust (cargo add a2a-lf). The a2a-samples repo shows it in action.
There is also a DeepLearning.AI course. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: A protocol, not a ready app
Needs agents on both sides to support it
